paragraphs.text: This is a [Zhengshan Xiaozhong](lapsang:definition), the [red tea](red:definition) of Tongmu village in the Wuyi Mountains, dated 1920. It was pine smoked the traditional way of the early Republican era. In that way the leaf dries over a fire of local pine in a [qinglou](lapsang:smoke), a wooden house of several floors with the fire at the bottom and the leaf on bamboo mats above, so the heat and smoke rise through it.

Tongmu sits on the high northern edge of the [Wuyi range](wuyi-mountains:two-teas), close to the Jiangxi border, in forested country that is now protected. It is the village usually given as the [birthplace of black tea](fujian:history). Its tea first reached Europe through Dutch and then British trade, under names such as [Bohea and Souchong](lapsang:history).

At a hundred and six years, this tea stands outside any named tradition. Lapsang has no recognised [tradition of long ageing](lapsang:ageing), and no category of red tea aged for decades is described.

brewing.text: In a cup or pot, use about 3 grams for 240 ml, with water at 90 to 100°C, and steep about two to five minutes, usually around three. Gongfu style, use about 5 grams in a 100 to 110 ml gaiwan or pot, with short steeps that grow a little longer each round. Too hot or too long and the smoke turns harsh and bitter and covers the tea.

notice.text: The smoke softer and further back, with dried fruit coming forward.
